# Building miniapps for AgentUI

A **miniapp** is a small web application you write — a **front** (React, in `src/`) and optional **handlers** (the server side, in `server/`) — that appears in the **Miniapps** tab of AgentUI. It runs inside AgentUI, uses its look and feel, and its data lives on the AgentUI server. Use it when the user wants a persistent tool (tracker, dashboard, list, calculator, small game…) rather than a one-off answer — for a one-off chart or table, use the `agentui_widget_chart` / `agentui_widget_table` widgets instead, and for a one-off interactive component (simulator, converter, filterable list…) use `agentui_widget_custom`, which takes a single TSX module written with the same UI kit.

## Workflow

1. `agentui_miniapp_create` — `id` (lowercase, digits, dashes, e.g. `habit-tracker`), `name`, `icon`, `description`.
2. `agentui_miniapp_write` — send all the files (several per call). The result tells you if the build succeeded; on `ok: false` read `errors` (file, line), fix, write again. The last working version stays online meanwhile.
3. Tell the user the miniapp is in the **Miniapps** tab (link: `/miniapps/<id>`). The miniapp updates live for anyone who has it open.
4. Iterate: `agentui_miniapp_read` / `agentui_miniapp_list` to see what exists, `agentui_miniapp_data` to read or push data (see below), `agentui_miniapp_logs` to see `console.log` output and handler errors, `agentui_miniapp_delete_file`, `agentui_miniapp_remove` (only on the user's request).

Icons for `icon`: apps, checklist, chart, calendar, notes, timer, shopping, finance, home, star, book, fitness, music, code, map, mail, photo, game, food, travel, weather, idea, health, tools.

## Files

```
src/main.tsx        REQUIRED — default-exports the root React component
src/*.tsx|ts|css    any other module (relative imports, `import './styles.css'`)
server/<route>.js   optional handlers (flat folder, .js or .ts)
```

Limits: 80 files, 512 KB per file, 4 MB total. Only `src/` (front) and `server/` (handlers) paths are accepted.

## Front (`src/`)

React 18 (automatic JSX runtime, no need to import React). Import everything from the provided modules — **there is no npm install**; other packages are not available:

- `react`, `react-dom/client`
- `@agentui/ui` — the UI kit and helpers below
- `chart.js` / `chart.js/auto` — for custom charts

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Page, Card, Stack, Row, Text, Button, TextField, List, ListItem, IconButton, Spinner, EmptyState, Alert, useApi, api, toast } from '@agentui/ui';

type Todo = { id: string; title: string; done: boolean };

export default function App() {
  const todos = useApi<Todo[]>('todos');
  const [title, setTitle] = useState('');
  const add = async () => {
    if (!title.trim()) return;
    await api.post('todos', { title });
    setTitle('');
    todos.reload();
  };
  return (
    <Page title="Todos">
      <Stack>
        <Row><TextField style={{ flex: 1 }} placeholder="New task" value={title} onChange={setTitle} onEnter={add} /><Button icon="add" onClick={add}>Add</Button></Row>
        {todos.loading && <Spinner center />}
        {todos.error && <Alert severity="error">{todos.error.message}</Alert>}
        {todos.data?.length === 0 && <EmptyState icon="checklist" title="Nothing to do" />}
        <Card padding={4}>
          <List>{todos.data?.map((t) => (
            <ListItem key={t.id} primary={t.title} trailing={<IconButton icon="delete" label="Delete" onClick={async () => { await api.delete(`todos/${t.id}`); todos.reload(); }} />} />
          ))}</List>
        </Card>
      </Stack>
    </Page>
  );
}
```

### Components (`@agentui/ui`)

| Component | Props |
|---|---|
| `Page` | `title?`, `actions?`, `maxWidth?` (default 860) — scrollable page with header. Use it as the root. |
| `Stack`, `Row` | `gap` (px, default 12), `align`, `justify`, `wrap`, `style`. `Row` = horizontal, centered. |
| `Card` | `padding?`, `onClick?` |
| `Text` | `variant`: `h5` `h6` `subtitle` `body` `caption` `overline`; `muted?`, `mono?` |
| `Divider` | |
| `Button` | `variant`: `contained`(default) `outlined` `text`; `color`: `primary` `danger` `neutral`; `size`: `small`; `icon?`; `loading?`; plus native button props |
| `IconButton` | `icon`, `label` (required, accessibility), `active?`, `onClick` |
| `Icon` | `name`, `size?` |
| `TextField` | `value`, `onChange(value: string)`, `label?`, `helperText?`, `error?`, `multiline?`, `rows?`, `type?`, `placeholder?`, `onEnter?` |
| `Select` | `value`, `onChange(value)`, `options: (string \| {value,label})[]`, `label?` |
| `Checkbox`, `Switch` | `checked`, `onChange(boolean)`, `label?` |
| `List`, `ListItem` | `primary`, `secondary?`, `leading?`, `trailing?`, `onClick?`, `selected?` |
| `Table` | `columns: {key,label,align?,render?(row)}[]`, `rows`, `onRowClick?` |
| `Tabs` | `value`, `onChange`, `tabs: {value,label}[]` |
| `Chip` | `label`, `color?`: `primary` `success` `warning` `danger`; `onDelete?` |
| `Alert` | `severity`: `info` `success` `warning` `error` |
| `Dialog` | `open`, `title?`, `onClose`, `actions?`, children |
| `Spinner` | `center?` |
| `EmptyState` | `icon?`, `title`, `description?`, `action?` |
| `Chart` | `type`: `line` `bar` `doughnut`; `labels: string[]`; `series: {name, data: number[]}[]`; `height?` — themed chart.js |

Icon names (`Icon`, `Button icon`, `IconButton icon`): add, close, check, delete, edit, search, refresh, back, forward, star, heart, info, warning, error, chevron-right, chevron-down, send, download, play, pause, more, home, person, apps, checklist.

Helpers: `useWidth()` → width in px available to the component (for `agentui_widget_custom` it is the chat bubble, about 250-330 px on a phone: size canvases and boards with it, never a fixed width); `requestFullscreen()` / `exitFullscreen()` / `useFullscreen()` / `useHeight()` (only for `agentui_widget_custom` in the chat: a miniapp already has its own page, the request just answers `false`); `toast(message)`; `openUrl(url)` (opens an external link in a new tab); `useTheme()` → `{ mode: 'light'|'dark', lang }`; `useLang()` → `'fr'` / `'en'`… (translate your texts for the user's language); `chartColors()` → palette for custom chart.js charts.

### Calling the handlers

`api.get(path)`, `api.post(path, body)`, `api.put`, `api.patch`, `api.delete` call **your own handlers** (`server/*.js`) — never an external URL. Paths are relative to the miniapp: `api.get('todos')` → `server/todos.js`, `api.get('todos/42')` → `server/todos.js` with `req.path === '/42'`. Failures throw `ApiError` (`message`, `status`). `useApi(path, deps?)` → `{ data, error, loading, reload, setData }` (pass `null` to skip).

### Look and feel — rules

The miniapp must look native. **Use the components above and the CSS variables; never hardcode colors, fonts or radii.** The theme (light/dark) changes at runtime.

- Variables: `--au-bg` (page), `--au-paper` (cards), `--au-raised` (inputs/hover), `--au-accent`, `--au-on-accent`, `--au-text`, `--au-muted`, `--au-line` (borders), `--au-danger`, `--au-success`, `--au-warning`, `--au-info`, `--au-radius` (12px), `--au-radius-sm`, `--au-font`, `--au-mono`.
- Custom CSS goes in a `.css` file imported from a module, referencing those variables: `border: 1px solid var(--au-line); background: var(--au-paper); border-radius: var(--au-radius);`.
- Base font size is 14px; spacing multiples of 4/8px. Design **mobile first** (see the section below): the miniapp is mostly used on a phone.
- The page itself does not scroll: `Page` scrolls internally. Do not use `100vh` tricks; fill the available space.
- No external resources in the front (images, fonts, scripts, CDN, direct `fetch` to the internet): the iframe is sandboxed and its CSP blocks them. Use inline SVG or `data:` URLs; fetch external data through `ctx.fetch` in a handler. For live data, refresh with `setInterval` + `api.get(...)` or `useApi`.
- External links: `window.open` and `target="_blank"` are blocked by the sandbox, so use `openUrl(url)` from `@agentui/ui` (or a plain `<a href="https://…">`, which is routed through it). The host opens it in a new tab; only `http(s):`, `mailto:` and `tel:` are accepted. Call it from a user action (click).
- No `localStorage`/cookies (opaque origin): persist through the handlers (`ctx.db` / `ctx.kv`).

### Mobile first

Users open miniapps on a phone at least as often as on a desktop. Design the narrow layout first (one column, 320–400 px wide), then enhance for wider screens — never the opposite.

- Start with a single column: `Stack` (vertical) as the page content, full-width `TextField` / `Select` / `Button`. Put side-by-side controls in a `Row` with `wrap` so they stack when there is no room.
- Keep `Page` as the root (it already limits width to 860 px and reduces padding on small screens). Do not set pixel widths on containers; use `flex: 1`, `min-width: 0` and percentages.
- Several columns only from a width threshold, in your CSS file:
  ```css
  .cards { display: grid; gap: 12px; grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
  @media (min-width: 700px) { .cards { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(240px, 1fr)); } }
  ```
- `Table` scrolls horizontally inside its container: keep few columns, or render a `List` / `Card` per row on small screens.
- Touch: targets ≥ 40 px (the provided `Button` / `IconButton` already are), spacing between tappable items, no interaction that exists only on hover (tooltips, hover menus), no tiny text (< 12 px).
- Long texts: let them wrap or truncate with ellipsis *and* make the full text reachable; avoid horizontal scrolling of the whole page.
- Charts: use `Chart` with a `height` around 200–240 and few labels; it adapts to the container width.
- Dialogs fit the screen (`Dialog` is limited to the viewport and scrolls); keep their content short.
- Test mentally (or with `getComputedStyle`) at 360 px wide before delivering.

## Handlers (`server/*.js`)

The handlers are the server side of the miniapp. Each file is a route. Export one **handler** function per HTTP method (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`); `server/index.js` handles everything no other file matches. A handler receives `(req, ctx)` and return any JSON-serializable value (or `ctx.status(code, body)`).

```js
// server/todos.js  →  /todos, /todos/<id>
export function GET(req, ctx) {
  const todos = ctx.db.collection('todos');
  if (req.path === '/') return todos.find({}, { sort: '_createdAt' });
  return todos.get(req.path.slice(1)) ?? ctx.status(404, { error: 'Not found' });
}
export function POST(req, ctx) {
  if (!req.body?.title) return ctx.status(400, { error: 'title is required' });
  return ctx.db.collection('todos').insert({ title: String(req.body.title), done: false });
}
export function PATCH(req, ctx) {
  return ctx.db.collection('todos').update(req.path.slice(1), req.body) ?? ctx.status(404, { error: 'Not found' });
}
export function DELETE(req, ctx) {
  ctx.db.collection('todos').remove(req.path.slice(1));
  return { ok: true };
}
```

- `ctx.status(code, body, headers?)` — answers with a status code, a body and, optionally, response headers. The body stays JSON by default; a string body with `Content-Type: text/html` (or `text/plain`) is sent as is. Only these headers are honored (names are case-insensitive): `location`, `content-type`, `cache-control`, `retry-after`. Any other is ignored and logged (`set-cookie`, `content-length` and `transfer-encoding` are always refused). Values must be strings of at most 1024 bytes without line breaks or control characters; at most 10 headers. A bad header is dropped, the request does not fail. Without headers, nothing changes. Documents (`text/html`, XML, SVG) are served sandboxed — no scripts, no access to the user's session — so they must be static (inline CSS is fine). Typical use, in `server/public.js`, an OAuth return that redirects to the miniapp page:
  ```js
  export async function GET(req, ctx) {
    if (req.path !== '/callback') return ctx.status(404, { error: 'Not found' });
    // …exchange req.query.code with ctx.fetch, store the token with ctx.kv.set…
    return ctx.status(302, null, { Location: '/miniapps/google-auth' });
  }
  // A page instead of a redirect:
  // return ctx.status(200, '<!doctype html><title>Done</title><p>You can close this tab.</p>', { 'Content-Type': 'text/html; charset=utf-8' });
  ```
- **Closing the tab after an external flow** (OAuth…): a link opened with `openUrl` lives in its own tab. Redirect to `/close.html?to=<url-encoded path>` — e.g. `ctx.status(302, null, { Location: '/close.html?to=%2Fminiapps%2Fgoogle-auth' })` — and the tab closes itself; if the browser refuses (the tab was not opened by a script), it shows a "Back to AgentUI" link to that same-origin path (`to` defaults to `/`; anything else is ignored).
- `req`: `{ method, path, query, body }` (`path` is relative to the route file: `/` or `/42`; in `server/index.js` it is the whole path).
- `ctx.db.collection(name)` — JSON documents, **synchronous** (no `await` needed): `find(filter?, { limit?, sort?, desc? })` (equality filter on top-level fields), `get(id)`, `insert(doc)` → doc with generated `id`, `_createdAt`, `_updatedAt`; `update(id, patch)` (merge, returns doc or `null`), `remove(id)` → boolean. Collection names: letters/digits/`_`/`-`. Data is private to the miniapp.
- `ctx.kv.get(key)`, `ctx.kv.set(key, value)`, `ctx.kv.delete(key)` — small settings/state.
- **Public handlers (webhooks)**: `server/public.js` is the only route reachable **without authentication**, at `https://<host>/public/<miniapp-id>/<path>` (e.g. `/public/github-notes/push`). Same shape as other handlers (`GET`…`DELETE` exports), with `req.path` = `/<path>`, `ctx.user === null`, plus `req.headers` (lower-case, no cookies) and `req.rawBody` (string, for signature checks). JSON and form bodies are parsed into `req.body`; other content types arrive as text. Nothing else in `server/` is ever public. Because anyone can call it: authenticate the caller yourself (secret stored with `ctx.kv.set('webhookSecret', …)` and checked against a header or a path segment, or an HMAC signature), validate everything, return `ctx.status(401, …)` otherwise, and never return private data. Rate limited to 120 requests/min per IP. Tell the user the full public URL.
- **Scheduled tasks of a miniapp**: when you create a cron job that feeds or serves a miniapp, create it with your usual scheduler tool, then tag it with `agentui_miniapp_job` (`action: 'link'`, `id`, `job_id`). AgentUI shows the link in the Tasks page and **deletes the tagged tasks when the miniapp is removed** (`unlink` drops the tag, `list` shows the tagged ids). Do it for every task that only makes sense with that miniapp.
- From outside the miniapp (cron, your own fetches), `agentui_miniapp_data` reads and writes the same collections and `kv` store; open miniapps refresh by themselves (`useApi` refetches silently).
- `ctx.user` — `{ id, username }` of the logged-in AgentUI user. All requests are authenticated by AgentUI (except `server/public.js`, below, where `ctx.user` is `null`).
- **Files and folders** (`ctx.fs`): a handler can touch the server's files only if they were declared when you registered the miniapp, with `agentui_miniapp_create` → `fs: [{ path: '/abs/folder', mode: 'ro' | 'rw' }]` (absolute paths; a folder covers its content; default `ro`). Paths must be under the folders the administrator allows (an error lists them; none configured = feature off), never AgentUI's own data. A grant is **inactive until the user approves it** in the miniapp header — tell them. Re-sending `fs` replaces the list; unchanged grants stay approved, new or widened ones (`ro` → `rw`) need approval again. Synchronous API on absolute paths: `ctx.fs.readFile(path, encoding?)` (utf8 default, or `'base64'`), `writeFile(path, content, encoding?)`, `readdir(path)` → `[{ name, type: 'file'|'dir'|'other', size }]`, `stat(path)` → `{ type, size, mtime }` or `null`, `mkdir(path)` (recursive), `remove(path)` (file or empty folder). Writes need `rw`; files ≤ 2 MB; symlinks cannot leave the grant. Without approval every call throws.
- **Crypto** (`ctx.crypto`, also available as the global `crypto`): synchronous, strings in / strings out. `hash(algo, data, enc?)` and `hmac(algo, key, data, enc?)` with `algo` in `md5`, `sha1`, `sha256`, `sha384`, `sha512` and `enc` = `'hex'` (default), `'base64'` or `'base64url'`; `randomBytes(n, enc?)` (1–1024 bytes); `randomUUID()`; `timingSafeEqual(a, b)` → boolean (use it to compare secrets and signatures, never `===`). Typical use: verify a webhook signature — `ctx.crypto.timingSafeEqual(req.headers['x-signature'], 'sha256=' + ctx.crypto.hmac('sha256', secret, req.rawBody))` — or generate a state / token for an OAuth flow. Signatures with a PEM key: `sign(alg, privateKeyPem, data, enc?)` → signature (default `'base64url'`, the JWT format) and `verify(alg, publicKeyPem, data, signature, enc?)` → boolean, with `alg` in `RS256|RS384|RS512` (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5), `PS256|PS384|PS512` (RSA-PSS), `ES256|ES384|ES512` (ECDSA, JWT r‖s format). `base64url(text)` / `fromBase64url(text)` convert UTF-8 text, to build a JWT: `const h = ctx.crypto.base64url(JSON.stringify({ alg: 'RS256', typ: 'JWT' })); const p = ctx.crypto.base64url(JSON.stringify(claims)); const jwt = h + '.' + p + '.' + ctx.crypto.sign('RS256', ctx.kv.get('privateKey'), h + '.' + p);` (e.g. a Google service-account token request via `ctx.fetch`). Keep private keys in `ctx.kv`, never in `src/`. No encryption (AES) and no key generation.
- `ctx.log(...)` / `console.log(...)` — visible with `agentui_miniapp_logs`.
- `await ctx.fetch(url, { method?, headers?, body? })` — calls an external HTTP(S) API from a handler → `{ status, ok, url, headers, text, json() }`. `body` may be an object (sent as JSON) or a string. Public addresses only: localhost, private networks and internal services are refused. Redirects are followed (3 max; `Authorization` is dropped when the origin changes). Limits: 15 s per call, 10 calls per request, 2 MB response. This is the **only** way to reach the internet: the front itself cannot (`api.get/post` only reach your own handlers), so a live-data miniapp fetches in a handler and returns the result.
- Secrets: never write an API key in `src/` (it ships to the browser). Keep it out of the front: store it with `ctx.kv.set('apiKey', …)` from a handler (or `agentui_miniapp_data` `kv_set`) and read it in `server/*.js` only.
- Sandbox: plain JavaScript (async/await allowed), no `require`/`import` of modules, no filesystem, no timers, no `eval`. CPU time is limited to 3 s per request (time waiting for the network does not count), 30 s in total. For slow or heavy work, poll from the front rather than holding one request open.
- Limits: documents ≤ 256 KB, 20 000 documents per miniapp, responses ≤ 2 MB.

## Checklist before telling the user it is ready

- `src/main.tsx` default-exports the component and the build returned `ok: true`.
- Handles loading, empty and error states (`Spinner`, `EmptyState`, `Alert`).
- Only `@agentui/ui` components / `--au-*` variables for styling; works in light and dark mode and is usable at 360 px wide (mobile first, no horizontal page scroll).
- Texts follow the user's language (`useLang()`), or the language you are talking in.
- Handlers validate input and return `ctx.status(400, …)` on bad requests.
